about: Recipes for ElevenLabs sound-effect source material (tools/audio/sfx_generate.py). Each source layers under one SfxSystem sound; tools/audio/sfx_layer.py mixes it with the synthesised transient into the shipped takes. Tone: cinematic exaggeration (the lead), guns that sound dangerous. Pilot first ("pilot": true), the lead listens, then the batch. The energy family (round 5, after the lead played the Syndicate) describes the physical event - capacitors, arc flash, superheated air - because prompting for a "laser" returns the 1950s ray gun and no mixing rescues it.

sources.prompt: A tank main gun firing, cinematic and huge: a sharp supersonic crack, a deep chest-thumping boom, then a long rolling thunder tail echoing off concrete stadium walls. Single shot, no music.
One single round from a heavy 25mm autocannon: a hard punchy thump with a metallic mechanical clank of the bolt, short slap echo off concrete. Exactly one shot.

A belt-fed heavy machine gun firing one long unbroken burst at close range: every round a hard supersonic crack over a deep chugging thump from the receiver, the bolt hammering, brass casings ringing off steel plate, the whole burst slapping back off the concrete walls of a huge arena. Relentless and frightening, steady rate, no pauses, no music.
An armor-piercing tank shell slamming into thick steel armor plate: a colossal metallic clang and crunch, shrapnel and debris, a ringing metal tail. Cinematic.
A heavy military energy weapon firing one pulse: a searing electric crack and a deep sizzling zap with a short hum decay. Gritty sci-fi, not cartoonish.
A mortar round launched from its tube: a deep hollow thoomp with a whoosh of propellant gas and a short echo. Single launch.
A military flamethrower spraying continuously: a roaring whoosh of burning fuel, turbulent crackling flame and hiss under pressure.
One single heavy machine gun round firing: a sharp dry crack with a mechanical knock. Exactly one shot, very short.
A large artillery shell whizzing past very close overhead: a tearing air rush and a falling doppler whistle.
A single bullet striking thick steel armor: a sharp metallic ping and spark crack. One hit, very short.
A bullet ricocheting off armor plate: a metallic tick and a zinging whine flying away. One ricochet.
A shell exploding into packed dirt and gravel: a heavy thud, a spray of earth and stones pattering down.
A shell punching straight through a tank's thin rear armor: a violent tearing metal crunch, sparks and a deep internal thump.
A projectile hitting an energy force field: a heavy electric thump with a crackling warbling shimmer. Gritty sci-fi.
An energy shield overloading and collapsing: a sputtering electrical failure, a descending power-down whine and a crackle.
A mid-size explosive round detonating against a vehicle: a sharp blast with metal debris and a short fiery tail.
An armored vehicle destroyed: a massive explosion, then a second blast as the ammunition cooks off, popping rounds, burning debris raining down, a long rumbling fire tail. Cinematic.

An electromagnetic rail launcher firing a steel slug: a huge capacitor bank discharging, a violent crack of superheated air tearing open, heavy metallic recoil, and a low electrical hum decaying under it. Brutal industrial machinery, not science fiction.

A high-power industrial cutting laser firing one pulse: an electrical arc flash cracking, superheated air hissing, metal vaporising, a transformer hum falling away. Dangerous and expensive, no pitch sweep.

A rapid-fire energy weapon firing continuously: a fast train of electrical arc discharges, ionised air crackling, a taut high-voltage hum underneath, capacitors recharging between shots. Mechanical and relentless.
A heavy energy cannon firing a single charged pulse: a capacitor thump you feel in the chest, an arc flash crack, a short ionised hiss afterwards. No zap, no whine.
A guided missile leaving its rail on a vehicle: the igniter cracking, a solid rocket motor roaring to life, the exhaust tearing away into the distance. No explosion.
A high-energy bolt striking thick steel armour: a violent electrical discharge into metal, steel flashing to vapour with a sharp crack, molten spatter and a crackling after-hiss.
A sonic weapon firing continuously: a deep pulsing subsonic throb with a hard metallic resonance on every pulse, air compressing and releasing, an oppressive low drone underneath.

Two heavy machine guns mounted side by side firing together in one long unbroken burst: a dense tearing roar of overlapping supersonic cracks faster than either gun alone, twin receivers hammering, a torrent of brass casings clattering on steel, echoing off concrete arena walls. Brutal, steady rate, no pauses, no music.
